extracted.intended_audience: Owners or operators of bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations (affected sources) required to comply with 40 CFR part 63 subpart R reporting and recordkeeping
extracted.subtask_description: Specific recordkeeping and reporting requirements that owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations must follow to demonstrate compliance with the emission limits, monitoring, testing, and work-practice standards in 40 CFR part 63 subpart R. Covers what to record, retention periods, report content, formats, and electronic submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record applicable CMS operating or emission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable operating or emission limit for the CMS. For combustion zone temperature operating limits, include the applicable date range the limit applies based on when the performance test was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record must indicate the specific operating or emission limit used by the CMS and, for combustion zone temperature limits, the date range tied to the performance test that established the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record CMS measurement values (combustion temp, pressure, TOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature measured by the temperature CPMS, each 5-minute average reading from the pressure CPMS, and each 3-hour rolling average total organic compounds (TOC) concentration (as propane) measured by the TOC CEMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuous records of these rolling/averaging values as reported by the monitoring systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record deviations of operating limits (start, duration, cause, corrective action)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deviation of the 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature operating limit, maximum loading pressure specified in § 60.502a(h), or 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration (as propane), the start date and time, duration, cause, and the corrective action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear narrative and timestamps describing the deviation cause and corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record CMS outages and out-of-control periods
rubrics_metrics.description: For each period when there was a CMS outage or the CMS was out of control, the start date and time, duration, cause, and the corrective action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TOC CEMS outages where the limited alternative for vapor recovery systems in § 60.504a(e) is used, the corrective action must include an indication of the use of that limited alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record inspections and calibrations of CMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inspection or calibration of the CMS including a unique identifier, make, and model number of the CMS, and date of calibration check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For TOC CEMS include the type of CEMS used (e.g., flame ionization detector, nondispersive infrared analyzer) and indicate whether methane is excluded from the TOC concentration reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC CEMS alternative outage historical cycle records
rubrics_metrics.description: For TOC CEMS outages where the limited alternative for vapor recovery systems in § 60.504a(e) is used, keep records of: (A) the quantity of liquid product loaded in gasoline cargo tanks for the past 10 adsorption cycles prior to the CEMS outage; (B) the vacuum pressure, purge gas quantities, and duration of the vacuum/purge cycles used for the past 10 desorption cycles prior to the CEMS outage; (C) the quantity of liquid product loaded in gasoline cargo tanks for each adsorption cycle while using the alternative; (D) the vacuum pressure, purge gas quantities, and duration of the vacuum/purge cycles for each desorption cycle while using the alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain both historical (prior 10 cycles) and ongoing cycle records when using the limited alternative during outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain pilot flame monitoring outputs for flares
rubrics_metrics.description: The output of the monitoring device used to detect the presence of a pilot flame as required in § 63.670(b) for a minimum of 2 years. Retain records of each 15-minute block during which there was at least one minute that no pilot flame is present when gasoline vapors were routed to the flare for a minimum of 5 years. The record must identify the start and end time and date of each 15-minute block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep continuous monitoring outputs for 2 years; keep flagged 15-minute blocks with absent pilot flame for 5 years with precise timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible emissions observation records (Method 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible emissions observations as specified for a minimum of 3 years. If using Method 22, the record must identify the date, the start and end time of the visible emissions observation, and the number of minutes for which visible emissions were observed during the observation. If observations are performed more than once in a day, include separate records for each observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Method 22 is not used for full 2-hour periods, special summary-estimate records are required (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record limited-duration visible emissions estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: For each 2-hour period for which visible emissions are observed for more than 5 minutes in 2 consecutive hours but visible emissions observations according to Method 22 were not conducted for the full 2-hour period, the record must include the date, the start and end time of the visible emissions observation, and an estimate of the cumulative number of minutes in the 2-hour period for which emissions were visible based on best information available to the owner or operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide best-available estimates and time bounds when full Method 22 coverage is not performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record 15-minute blocks when operating values outside limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each 15-minute block period during which operating values are outside of the applicable operating limits specified in § 63.670(d) through (f) when liquid product is being loaded into gasoline cargo tanks for at least 15-minutes identifying the specific operating limit that was not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which operating limit was exceeded/missed and maintain 15-minute block timestamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record 15-minute block average cumulative flows and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The 15-minute block average cumulative flows for the thermal oxidation system vent gas or flare vent gas and, if applicable, total steam, perimeter assist air, and premix assist air specified to be monitored, along with the date and start and end time for the 15-minute block. If multiple monitoring locations are used, retain records of the 15-minute block average flows for each monitoring location for a minimum of 2 years, and retain the 15-minute block average cumulative flows that are used in subsequent calculations for a minimum of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pressure and temperature monitoring is used, also retain 15-minute block average temperature, pressure, and molecular weight records for 2 years and cumulative flows used in calculations for 5 years. Supplemental gas flow rate records (winter/summer if applicable) must be retained for 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain vent gas composition analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The thermal oxidation system vent gas or flare vent gas compositions specified to be monitored; retain records of individual component concentrations from each compositional analysis for a minimum of 2 years. If NHV analyzer is used, retain records of the 15-minute block average values for a minimum of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If demonstrating consistent composition per § 63.670(j)(6), retain records of the required minimum ratio of gasoline loaded to total liquid product loaded and the actual ratio on a 15-minute block basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain minimum gasoline loading rate records
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, retain records of the required minimum gasoline loading rate as specified in § 60.502a(c)(3)(vii) and the actual gasoline loading rate on a 15-minute block basis for a minimum of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applicable where that minimum gasoline loading rate requirement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record 15-minute block average operating parameters (per §63.670(k)-(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each 15-minute block average operating parameter calculated following the methods specified in § 63.670(k) through (n), as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced methods to calculate and record these operating parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record periods when monitoring procedures not followed
rubrics_metrics.description: All periods during which the owner or operator does not perform monitoring according to the procedures in § 63.670(g), (i), and (j) or in § 60.502a(c)(3)(vii) and (viii) as applicable. Note the start date, start time, and duration in minutes for each period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document every occurrence of out-of-procedure monitoring with precise timestamps and durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record whether 'vapors displaced' excludes certain loading periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of whether “vapors displaced from gasoline cargo tanks during product loading” excludes periods when liquid product is loaded but no gasoline cargo tanks are being loaded or if liquid product loading is assumed to be loaded into gasoline cargo tanks according to § 60.502a(c)(3)(i), and keep records of all time periods when "vapors displaced from gasoline cargo tanks during product loading" and records of time periods when there were no such vapors displaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the interpretation used and keep continuous time-period records for both inclusions and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain one-time flare tip velocity compliance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If you comply with the flare tip velocity operating limit using the one-time flare tip velocity operating limit compliance assessment as provided in § 60.502a(c)(3)(ix), maintain records of the applicable one-time flare tip velocity operating limit compliance assessment for as long as you use this compliance method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the assessment documentation for the duration the compliance method is employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified CMS parameter record requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each parameter monitored using a CMS, retain for deviations: (A) For each deviation, record the start date and time, duration, cause, and corrective action taken. (B) For each period when there is a CMS outage or the CMS is out of control, record the start date and time, duration, cause, and corrective action taken. (C) Each inspection or calibration of the CMS including a unique identifier, make, and model number of the CMS, and date of calibration check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consolidates the CMS-specific deviation/outage/inspection recordkeeping across parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record all 5-minute loading interval statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of all 5-minute time periods during which liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks or assumed to be loaded into gasoline cargo tanks and records of all 5-minute time periods when there was no liquid product loaded into gasoline cargo tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuous 5-minute resolution records indicating loading status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep written procedures and previous performance evaluation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep written procedures required under § 63.8(d)(2) on record for the life of the affected source or until the affected source is no longer subject to the provisions of this part. If the performance evaluation plan is revised, keep previous (superseded) versions on record to be made available for inspection for 5 years after each revision. The program of corrective action shall be included in the plan as required under § 63.8(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain current and superseded plans per the specified retention periods and make them available upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage vessel recordkeeping and LEL monitoring records
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator of storage vessels shall keep records as specified in § 60.115b, except records shall be kept for at least 5 years. Additionally, for each storage vessel complying with § 63.423(b)(2), keep records of each LEL monitoring event including: (1) Date and time of the LEL monitoring and the storage vessel; (2) Description of the monitoring event; (3) Wind speed at the top of the storage vessel; (4) The LEL meter manufacturer and model and tubing details if used; (5) Calibration checks before and after measurements with gas used, Certificate of Analysis, results, and corrective action; (6) Location of measurements and floating roof; (7) Each measurement (taken at least once every 15 seconds) indicating whether automatic correction applied and raw & corrected measurements plus correction factor if not auto-corrected; (8) Each 5-minute rolling average reading; (9) If vapor concentration above 25% LEL on a 5-minute rolling average, description whether floating roof was repaired, replaced, or taken out of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain high-frequency raw data and calibration documentation; retention minimums apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak logbook entries (per §63.424(b) leaks detected)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each leak detected record in the logbook: (i) equipment type and identification number; (ii) the nature of the leak (vapor or liquid) and the method of detection (sight, sound, or smell); (iii) the date the leak was detected and the date of each attempt to repair; (iv) repair methods applied in each attempt to repair the leak; (v) 'Repair delayed' and the reason for the delay if not repaired within 15 calendar days; (vi) the expected date of successful repair of the leak if not repaired within 15 days; and (vii) the date of successful repair of the leak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a comprehensive repair history for each leak with reasons and expected completion dates when repairs are delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment inventory and leak inspection records
rubrics_metrics.description: For § 63.424(c) or § 60.503a(a)(2) inspections keep records of: (i) types, identification numbers, and locations of all equipment in gasoline service; (ii) for each leak inspection, an indication if conducted under § 63.424(c) or § 60.503a(a)(2) and the leak determination method used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an up-to-date equipment inventory and tie each inspection to the statutory inspection provision and method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 21 inspection record details
rubrics_metrics.description: For Method 21 inspections keep: (A) Date of inspection; (B) Inspector name; (C) Monitoring instrument identification; (D) Identification of all equipment surveyed and the instrument reading for each piece; (E) Date and time of instrument calibration and initials of operator performing the calibration; (F) Calibration gas cylinder identification, certification date, and certified concentration; (G) Instrument scale used; (H) Results of the daily calibration drift assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain full instrument and calibration traceability for Method 21 surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: OGI inspection records
rubrics_metrics.description: For leak inspections conducted with OGI, keep the records specified in section 12 of appendix K to part 60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow appendix K section 12 for the full list of required OGI records (including video retention where specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record details for each leak identified during inspections or routine duties
rubrics_metrics.description: For each leak detected during a leak inspection or by audio/visual/olfactory methods during normal duties, record: (A) equipment type and identification number; (B) the date the leak was detected, the name of the person who found the leak, nature of the leak and method of detection; (C) the date of each attempt to repair and methods applied; (D) the date of successful repair, the method of monitoring used to confirm the repair, and if Method 21 used the maximum instrument reading measured; if OGI used to confirm, keep video footage of the repair confirmation; (E) for each repair delayed beyond 15 calendar days record 'Repair delayed', reason, and expected date and signatory of decision-maker; (F) for leaks not repairable, the maximum instrument reading at time determined not repairable, OGI video showing emissions still visible, or signed record that leak is still detectable via audio/visual/olfactory methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document finder, repair confirmation method, and provide signed records where delays or non-repairability occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation reporting for bulk gasoline terminals and breakout stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator shall keep records for each deviation of an emissions limitation (including operating limit), work practice standard, or operation and maintenance requirement: (1) Date, start time, and duration of each deviation; (2) List of affected sources or equipment for each deviation, an estimate of the quantity of each regulated pollutant emitted over any emission limit and a description of the method used to estimate the emissions; (3) Actions taken to minimize emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-deviation documentation including emission-estimation methodology and mitigation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic records via CEDRI permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Any records required to be maintained by this subpart that are submitted electronically via the EPA Compliance and Emissions Data Reporting Interface (CEDRI) may be maintained in electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic retention does not affect obligation to make records available for inspection upon request by Administrator or delegated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test and evaluation record retention (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of each performance test or performance evaluation conducted and each notification and report submitted to the Administrator for at least 5 years. For each performance test, include indication of whether liquid product loading is assumed to be loaded into gasoline cargo tanks or excluded in the determination of the combustion zone temperature operating limit. If complying with the alternative in § 63.427(f), include pressure every 5 minutes while a gasoline cargo tank is being loaded and the highest instantaneous pressure that occurs during each loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep full performance test datasets, assumptions, and monitoring details for 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and format for performance test reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to Nov 4, 2024 submit performance test reports per § 63.13. Beginning Nov 4, 2024, within 60 days after completing each performance test and each CEMS performance evaluation, submit results following § 63.9(k). Include the combustion zone temperature operating parameter limit value set based on your performance test. If using monitoring alternative in § 63.427(f), indicate usage, identify loading racks, and report highest instantaneous pressure per rack. Data collected using test methods supported by EPA's Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT) must be submitted in ERT-generated file format or an XML schema listed on the ERT website; data from methods not supported by ERT must be included as an attachment in the ERT or alternate electronic file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with ERT format requirements when supported; otherwise attach unsupported data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Compliance Status submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit all Notification of Compliance Status reports in PDF format to the EPA following § 63.9(k), except mailed submissions must be sent to the attention of the Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission replaces physical signature where submitted via CEDRI (electronic signature in submission process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-May-8-2027 reporting: equipment inventory and instrument program
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator subject to § 63.424 shall report to the Administrator a description of the types, identification numbers, and locations of all equipment in gasoline service. For facilities electing an instrument program under § 63.424(b)(4), the report shall contain a full description of the program. Submission timing depends on whether source startup was before Dec 14, 1994 or later (different deadlines specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit inventory with Notification of Compliance Status for existing sources unless extension granted; new sources submit with application for approval of construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual reporting items (pre-May-8-2027) for leak and documentation events
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator shall include in a semiannual report: (i) Each loading of a gasoline cargo tank for which vapor tightness documentation had not been previously obtained; (ii) Periodic reports specified in § 60.115b; (iii) The number of equipment leaks not repaired within 5 days after detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts and instances as specified for the semiannual reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess emissions reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator shall submit an excess emissions report in accordance with § 63.10(e)(3) including occurrences such as: (i) Each exceedance or failure to maintain the monitored operating parameter value with monitoring data and description/timing of repair steps; (ii) Each instance of a nonvapor-tight gasoline cargo tank loading with failure to prevent reloading before documentation obtained; (iii) Each reloading of a nonvapor-tight cargo tank before documentation obtained; (iv) For leaks with no repair attempt within 5 days or not completed within 15 days include dates of detection and repair attempts, reasons for delay, and date of successful repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed monitoring data, narrative of remedial actions, and dates for each excess emissions event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility parameters documentation and annual reporting (facilities meeting §63.420(c)/(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For facilities meeting criteria in § 63.420(c) document and report methods/procedures/assumptions supporting calculations for determining criteria, maintain records that facility parameters have not been exceeded, report annually that parameters have not been exceeded, and allow modification requests with documentation of expected HAP emission change. For § 63.420(d) facilities, document use of emission screening equations and calculations and notify Administrator of any parameter modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make these documents available for public inspection and submit within the regulatory deadlines (some dates specified as historical but requirement remains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual report content on or after May 8, 2027 (facility general information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report general facility information: facility name, physical address (city/county/state), latitude/longitude in decimal degrees with at least five decimal places, contact person information (name, mailing address, phone, email), facility type (bulk gasoline terminal or pipeline breakout station), date of report and reporting period start/end dates, and a statement by a responsible official certifying truth/accuracy/completeness with name/title/signature (electronic signature via CEDRI substitutes for signature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise coordinates and a certifying official for each semiannual submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual CMS deviation reporting items (post-May-8-2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance when temperature CPMS measured 3-hour rolling averages below limit, pressure CPMS exceeded maximum loading pressure, or TOC CEMS measured 3-hour rolling average concentrations higher than the emission limitation, report: (A) Date and start time of deviation; (B) Duration in hours; (C) Each 3-hour rolling average value, and indicate whether methane is excluded for TOC; (D) Unique identifier for the CMS; (E) Make, model number, and date of last calibration check; (F) Cause and corrective action. Also report outages/out-of-control events with similar identifying information and corrective actions; if limited alternative used include indication and counts of types of deviations during use of alternative (adsorption/desorption cycles counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-event CMS identifiers, calibration info, and counts for alternative-use deviations as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual reporting for flares/thermal oxidizers (post-May-8-2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report dates and times for (A) each 15-minute block with at least one minute when vapors routed to flare and no pilot flame present; (B) each 2-hour period when visible emissions exceeded a total of 5 minutes with minutes observed or estimated; (C) each 15-minute period when applicable operating limits were not met and identify which limit; for (C)(1)-(3) provide additional subgrouped data depending on monitoring alternative used (loading rate ratios, supplemental gas flow rates, or net heating value operating parameter values). Also report start/date/time/duration for periods when vapors were routed to flare and monitoring not performed, and for CMS-related events include unique identifier, make/model/date of last calibration, cause and corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include blocks, durations, and, when using alternatives, the numeric ratios/flow rates or calculated operating parameters as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report cargo tanks without vapor tightness documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For any instance where liquid product was loaded into a gasoline cargo tank for which vapor tightness documentation was not provided or available, report cargo tank owner and address, cargo tank identification number, date/time of loading, and date proper documentation was received or statement that it was never received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide owner/address and timeline for documentation receipt or absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report improper filling/connection events
rubrics_metrics.description: For each instance when liquid product was loaded into gasoline cargo tanks not using submerged filling, not equipped with compatible vapor collection equipment, or not properly connected, report the date/time, type of deviation (e.g., not submerged filling, incompatible equipment, not properly connected), and cargo tank identification number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identification and deviation type for each improper loading event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate leak inspection and delay-of-repair reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report for each leak inspection required and leaks identified: (i) For leak inspections, date, leak determination method (OGI or Method 21), total number and type of equipment with leaks detected, total number/type repaired within 15 days, total number/type for which no repair attempt was made within 5 calendar days, total number/type placed on delay of repair. (ii) For leaks identified by audio/visual/olfactory methods during normal duties, report totals repaired within 15 days, totals with no repair attempt within 5 days, totals placed on delay of repair. (iii) Total number of leaks on the delay-of-repair list at start and end of reporting period. (iv) For each leak on the delay-of-repair list at any time, report unique equipment ID, type, leak determination method, reason(s) repair not feasible within 15 days, and if applicable the date repair was completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both aggregated counts and per-item delay-of-repair details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline storage vessel reporting (post-May-8-2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each gasoline storage vessel subject to § 63.423 report the information specified in § 60.115b or deviations in measured parameter values from the plan, or information specified in § 63.1066(b). For § 63.423(b)(2) deviations in LEL monitoring report date/start/end times, vessel identity, description of monitoring event, wind speed, highest 5-minute rolling average during event, and whether floating roof was repaired/replaced/taken out of service; if repaired/replaced include re-monitoring information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced sections to determine which data elements to include for the storage vessel and LEL deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of no deviations option
rubrics_metrics.description: If there were no deviations from the emission limitations, operating parameters, or work practice standards during the reporting period, provide a statement that there were no deviations. If no CMS was inoperable or out-of-control, provide a statement that there were no such periods during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A signed or electronically certified statement suffices when there are zero deviations or CMS downtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirement and timeline for semiannual reports (CEDRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning on May 8, 2027, or once the report template for this subpart has been available on the CEDRI website for one year (whichever is later), submit all subsequent semiannual compliance reports using the appropriate electronic report template on the CEDRI website following § 63.9(k), except mailed media must be sent to Gasoline Distribution Sector Lead. Unless an alternative schedule is approved, submit by the deadlines in the subpart regardless of submission method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor CEDRI for template availability and use the template when required; ensure timely submission even if template not yet available but Administrator has approved different schedule.
